activities.name: Chess.com Daily Chess (Correspondence)
activities.one_liner: A single chess game played by daily-chess rules where each partner has 1-3 days per move, so the 7-hour gap becomes the game's actual clock instead of an obstacle.
how_it_works: Asynchronous — no live session required; each partner logs in independently to make a move.
Both create free Chess.com accounts and add each other as friends via username search.
One challenges the other to a 'Daily' game (not Live/Rapid) with a 1-3 day time control per move.
Each checks the app whenever convenient — he moves at 6am before work, she answers at 11pm before bed — with push notifications on 'your turn.'
Multiple daily games can run in parallel, and Chess.com tracks a separate Daily rating so the relationship builds its own ongoing record.
tools_needed: Chess.com app or website (both partners), free account
activities.timezone_friction: A move takes under a minute and can be made at any point in either person's day — this is the purest expression of the 7h gap becoming the game's clock rather than a scheduling conflict. Tagged only to thin/asymmetric windows because that is its designed use case, not w1/w5/w6/w7 where a live game would be a better use of shared time.

activities.name: Words With Friends 2
activities.one_liner: Zynga's asynchronous Scrabble-style word game where up to 40 simultaneous games run in the background of daily life, each turn triggered by a push notification.
how_it_works: Asynchronous — no live session required.
Both download Words With Friends 2 (free) and connect via Facebook, Game Center, or an in-app friend code.
Start a match; the app allows roughly a 10-12 day-per-turn window so neither side ever feels rushed.
A push notification fires the moment it's your turn — play it standing in line, at a desk, or in bed.
Keep several games running at once for a low-grade constant thread of contact between calls.
tools_needed: Words With Friends 2 app (iOS), free account
activities.timezone_friction: Same mechanic as chess.com — a turn is a 2-5 minute task doable at any point in either day, so it lives entirely inside the thin/asymmetric windows rather than needing scheduled overlap.

activities.name: Wordfeud
activities.one_liner: A cleaner, less-monetized Scrabble-style correspondence game allowing up to 30 simultaneous games with a firm 72-hour-per-move forfeit clock.
how_it_works: Asynchronous — no live session required.
Both install Wordfeud (free) and add each other by username or from contacts.
Start a match; each player has up to 72 hours to play a move before forfeiting.
Push notifications alert the other partner the moment a move lands.
The firmer 72-hour clock (vs. WWF2's looser ~10-12 days) makes it a slightly higher-commitment ritual — good for a couple who wants a daily nudge rather than letting a game go stale for a week.
activities.timezone_friction: Same asynchronous-turn mechanic as WWF2/chess.com; the tighter 72-hour window is a deliberate variant for a couple who wants more daily pressure to check in, still well inside any single thin window.

activities.name: GamePigeon Asynchronous Board Games (Chess, Checkers, Four in a Row, Gomoku, Reversi, Dots and Boxes, Mancala)
activities.one_liner: The zero-friction option — seven no-timer, turn-based board games built directly into their existing iMessage thread, so playing a turn looks identical to sending a text.
how_it_works: Asynchronous — a move is sent as an iMessage attachment; the other partner is notified like a normal text and can respond whenever.
In an existing iMessage conversation, tap the apps icon in the message bar and open GamePigeon (free, install once).
Pick a game — Chess, Checkers, Four in a Row, Gomoku, Reversi, Dots and Boxes, or Mancala — and send the opening move.
The other partner sees it appear as a message bubble; tapping it opens the board to respond, no separate app-switch required.

Because it lives inside the same thread as their normal texting, it is the single most discreet, no-setup option in this entire library — usable at a desk, in a meeting, anywhere a phone glance is normal.
tools_needed: GamePigeon (free iMessage extension, both on iOS)
activities.timezone_friction: No live presence required and no app-switch beyond the Messages thread they already use daily — this is the best-case W4 entry in the whole library because it is indistinguishable from ordinary texting if she needs to close it instantly.

activities.name: Splendor Duel on Board Game Arena (Turn-Based Mode)
activities.one_liner: A 2-exclusive redesign of Splendor (gem-collecting card game) played turn-based on Board Game Arena, where BGA's adjustable 'moves per day' setting lets the couple set their own pace.
how_it_works: Asynchronous — BGA's turn-based mode means neither partner needs to be online simultaneously; you're notified by email/site when it's your turn.
Both create free Board Game Arena accounts and add each other as friends.
Start a Splendor Duel table (built for exactly 2 players, unlike the original 2-4 player Splendor) in 'turn-based' speed mode.
Set the game-speed option (e.g., '1 move per day') so BGA adapts the per-move time limit to the couple's actual pace.
Each takes their turn whenever convenient; the game persists across days without either partner losing their spot.
tools_needed: Board Game Arena account (both), boardgamearena.com or BGA app
activities.timezone_friction: BGA's turn-based speed setting exists specifically to decouple the game from real-time overlap, so it slots into any thin/asymmetric window. Unverified whether Splendor Duel specifically requires BGA's paid Premium tier ($3/mo) — flagged in gaps.

activities.name: Duolingo Friends Clash
activities.one_liner: A weekly head-to-head 1v1 XP battle inside Duolingo where two friends' independent daily lesson output is tallied directly against each other, resetting every week.
how_it_works: Asynchronous — each partner's individual lessons throughout the week count toward the head-to-head total; no live session required.
Both need active Duolingo accounts (they don't need to be learning the same language) and must add each other as in-app Friends.
Opt into Friends Clash when it appears as a weekly mode in Duolingo's Leagues/social tab.
Each partner's daily lesson XP is tallied automatically against the other's for that week.
Whoever accumulates more XP by the week's end wins the Clash; a new one starts the following week, creating a recurring rivalry.
activities.timezone_friction: XP accrues from ordinary daily lessons done independently at any hour, so the weekly total is timezone-blind by design. Confidence medium because the primary source is a dedicated fan-tracking site rather than Duolingo's own blog, though it corroborates the well-documented Leagues/Friends system.

activities.name: Duolingo Friend Streak
activities.one_liner: A streak counter shared between two Duolingo friends that only increases when BOTH complete a lesson that calendar day, turning language practice into a small daily mutual-accountability ritual.
how_it_works: Asynchronous — each does their own lesson at their own time; the streak just tracks that both showed up that day.
Both need Duolingo accounts and must add each other as Friends in-app (invite must be accepted).
Either partner can propose starting a Friend Streak from the friend's profile.
The Friend Streak increases by 1 only on days both partners complete at least one lesson.
A missed day by either side breaks the shared streak, which is the point — it's a gentle mutual-accountability nudge, not a solo habit tracker.
activities.timezone_friction: Because the streak only checks 'did you do a lesson today' per each person's own calendar day, the 7h offset and the mismatched work week are irrelevant — it is defined per-person, not per-shared-moment.

activities.name: Heads Up! via Apple SharePlay
activities.one_liner: The charades-style word-guessing app played live over FaceTime using native SharePlay — one partner holds the phone to their forehead while the other calls out clues over the same call.
how_it_works: Real-time — requires both live on the same FaceTime call, roughly 5-10 minutes for a full deck of rounds (60 seconds per word).
One partner needs the Heads Up! app installed ($1.99); it does not need to be installed on both devices for SharePlay to work.
Start or join a FaceTime call, tap the SharePlay control, and select Heads Up! from the available apps.
The guesser holds the phone up (screen facing away, word visible to the other partner over video) and the other calls out verbal clues; tilt the phone down for correct, up for pass.
Swap roles each round; extra categories (movies, accents, impressions) are sold as in-app purchases.
tools_needed: Heads Up! app (one partner, $1.99), FaceTime with SharePlay
activities.timezone_friction: Requires speaking clues at normal volume, which rules it out for W4's discretion requirement, and requires a live moment together, ruling out the correspondence-style thin windows — but it's a strong low-effort SharePlay-native option for W1 (playful before bed), W5, and W7.

activities.name: GamePigeon Timed Word Games (Word Hunt, Word Bites, Anagrams)
activities.one_liner: Fast, silent, timed word-search and anagram games inside iMessage where each partner plays their own timed run whenever convenient and the app compares scores.
how_it_works: Asynchronous — a challenge is sent as an iMessage attachment; each partner plays their own individually-timed round (not required to be live at the same moment) whenever they open it.
From an existing iMessage thread, open GamePigeon (already installed) and pick Word Hunt, Word Bites, or Anagrams.
Send the challenge; the other partner taps it to start their own timed round against the identical letter grid/tiles.
The app shows who scored higher once both have played their run.
A full round trip (send, they play, results appear) takes 2-5 minutes total and needs no talking, just taps.
tools_needed: GamePigeon (free iMessage extension, both on iOS)
activities.timezone_friction: Entirely silent and text-thread-native — she can play a 90-second round at her desk without audio or a hard commitment to a live partner moment, which is why this is one of the strongest W4 entries despite each round having its own internal timer.

activities.name: GamePigeon Quick Arcade Minigames (8-Ball, Mini Golf, Darts, Basketball, Cup Pong, Archery, Sea Battle, Knockout, Shuffleboard, Filler, Crazy 8, Tanks, 9-Ball)
activities.one_liner: A bundle of short, silent, physics-based iMessage minigames — pool, mini golf, darts, a Battleship variant — each playable in a handful of asynchronous turns without needing a live call.
how_it_works: Asynchronous — each shot/turn is sent as a message and answered whenever, though individual turns are quick physical/aiming actions (flick to putt, aim to shoot) rather than strategic board moves.
Open GamePigeon from an existing iMessage thread (already installed from the board-games entry above).
Pick a minigame — 8-Ball and 9-Ball (pool), Mini Golf, Darts, Basketball, Cup Pong, Archery, Sea Battle (a Battleship variant), Knockout, Shuffleboard, Filler, Crazy 8 (a card game), or Tanks.
Take a turn (aim and flick/tap) and send it; the other partner is notified and takes theirs whenever convenient.
Most of these have a natural short ending (best of 3 in pool, 9 holes in mini golf, sink the fleet in Sea Battle) making them good clean-stop options.
tools_needed: GamePigeon (free iMessage extension, both on iOS)
activities.timezone_friction: Same discreet, no-audio, glance-at-phone profile as the board games and word games above — the whole GamePigeon library shares this property, which is why it dominates this thread's W4 answer.

activities.name: skribbl.io Private Room
activities.one_liner: A free browser-based drawing-and-guessing game (like Pictionary) where the host creates a private room, sets it to exactly 2 players, and shares a link — no install, no account.
how_it_works: Real-time — both need to be online simultaneously in the same browser room; typically paired with an open FaceTime call for reactions, though guessing itself happens by typing in-browser.
One partner goes to skribbl.io and clicks 'Create Private Room.'
In room settings, set player count to 2 (the host can set anywhere from 2 to 20) and adjust draw time/rounds/word difficulty.
Share the generated room link (e.g., over iMessage) — the other partner clicks it and joins directly, no signup.
Players alternate drawing while the other types guesses in the in-browser chat; a full game runs about 15-25 minutes depending on round count.
tools_needed: Web browser (both), skribbl.io — no account or install
activities.timezone_friction: Needs simultaneous presence and full visual attention (watching a drawing appear stroke by stroke), so it does not survive W3's hands-busy constraint, but a short room (fewer rounds, shorter draw time) can fit inside W4's 60-minute hard bound if she can spare full screen attention at her desk.

activities.name: PlayingCards.io Virtual Tabletop (Backgammon or Checkers)
activities.one_liner: A free browser-based virtual tabletop that recreates real card/board games (including 2-player classics like backgammon and checkers) with live drag-and-drop pieces synced between browsers — no app install for either partner.
how_it_works: Real-time — both need to be online simultaneously, moving pieces live on a shared synced board while talking over FaceTime.
One partner goes to playingcards.io, picks a game from the library (e.g., backgammon, checkers, or a standard 52-card deck to build any card game), and clicks Start to generate a private room.
Share the room code or link with the other partner, who joins via the site — no install or login needed on either side.
Drag pieces/cards on the shared virtual table; all movements sync live for both players.
Works on phone browsers but is easier to read on a laptop or tablet given the amount of on-screen detail.
tools_needed: Web browser (both), playingcards.io — no account or install
activities.timezone_friction: A live, both-present, full-screen-attention activity, so it only fits windows where both are free and unhurried; not tagged to any thin window because dragging pieces on a small screen is a poor fit for a hands-busy or hard-stop constraint.

activities.name: Codenames: Duet (Online)
activities.one_liner: The official cooperative 2-player redesign of Codenames — built from scratch for exactly two people, unlike the original 4-player team version — playable in a browser instead of needing two physical decks.
how_it_works: Real-time — both partners play live together, each seeing their own half of a shared 5x5 word grid and giving one-word clues out loud over the call.

Codenames: Duet is a specific ruleset (not the same as base Codenames, which needs two teams of 2+); confirm the online version played implements Duet, since most default web implementations run classic team-mode Codenames instead.
One partner sets up an online room implementing Duet mode and shares the link with the other.

Each partner sees a keycard showing 9 of the 25 words as their own 'agents' — neither has the full picture — and takes turns giving a one-word clue plus a number to help the other find agents without hitting the assassin.
The pair has a shared 9-turn budget to find all the agents; a full game runs about 15-20 minutes.
tools_needed: Web browser (both), a Codenames-online implementation with Duet mode enabled
activities.timezone_friction: Cooperative rather than competitive, and low-pressure enough to work even when one partner is winding down for bed (w1) — but still needs live simultaneous presence, so it is not a thin-window fit.

activities.name: GeoGuessr Duels (Private Party)
activities.one_liner: A live head-to-head geography-guessing game — both look at the same Street View image and race to pinpoint the location on a map, with points based on accuracy and speed.
how_it_works: Real-time — both need to be online simultaneously for a live round-based match, typically 15-20 minutes for a full Duel.
Both need free GeoGuessr accounts (unlimited/ranked Duels access commonly requires the paid Pro tier — see cost note).
One partner selects 'Play with Friends,' creates a private party, and shares the invite link.
Choose 'Duels' mode with custom settings (map pack, time limit, health-based scoring) for a private 1v1 match.
Each round, both see the same location and drop a guess pin against the clock; damage is dealt based on guess accuracy, and the first to reduce the other's health to zero wins the round.
tools_needed: GeoGuessr account (both), geoguessr.com or iOS app
activities.cost: cheap (free tier limited; Pro ~$3.99-6.99/mo often required for full Duels access)
activities.timezone_friction: A live, screen-dependent, both-present game with no natural mid-round pause — fits evening/weekend windows where neither has a hard stop, not the thin windows.

activities.name: Exploding Kittens (Netflix Games)
activities.one_liner: The viral card game (draw cards, avoid the exploding kitten, use action cards to mess with your opponent) available free within Netflix Games for 2-5 players — both partners just need their own Netflix subscriptions.
how_it_works: Real-time — both need to be online simultaneously in the same online game session; a round runs roughly 10-15 minutes.
Both need active Netflix subscriptions (separate accounts are fine) and the Exploding Kittens app under Netflix Games on iOS.
One partner starts an online multiplayer game from within the app.
The other joins using their own Netflix sign-in — both must be Netflix customers to play together online, and up to five total players can join a game.
Standard Exploding Kittens rules apply: draw cards each turn, avoid pulling an exploding kitten (or defuse it), use action cards (Attack, Skip, Favor, Shuffle, See the Future) to control the deck.
tools_needed: Netflix subscription (both, separate accounts fine), Exploding Kittens app under Netflix Games
activities.cost: paid (requires an active Netflix subscription each, roughly $7-$25/mo depending on plan; exact Israel-vs-US pricing not independently re-verified this session)
activities.timezone_friction: A quick, mostly-tap-based round with light required chat, so it can survive a lunch-break W4 slot if both happen to be free at the same moment — though it still needs true simultaneous presence, unlike the correspondence games above.

activities.name: 7 Wonders Duel on Board Game Arena (Real-Time Mode)
activities.one_liner: A civilization-building card game redesigned to be playable by exactly two people, played live (not turn-based) on Board Game Arena.
how_it_works: Real-time — both partners need to be online simultaneously; unlike Splendor Duel above, this is designed for a live 30-45 minute session, not correspondence play.
Both need free Board Game Arena accounts (whether this specific title requires BGA's paid Premium tier is unconfirmed — see gaps).
One invites the other directly to a table for '7 Wonders Duel,' played in real-time speed mode.

Players draft cards from a shared pyramid-shaped tableau across three ages, racing toward military, science, or civilian victory — a game built from scratch for exactly two, not a scaled-down multiplayer game.
A single game runs ~30-45 minutes with no natural pause point, so treat it as a single-block Saturday or evening activity rather than something to interrupt.
tools_needed: Board Game Arena account (both), boardgamearena.com or BGA app
activities.cost: free (Premium tier requirement for this specific title unverified)
activities.timezone_friction: Requires full simultaneous attention for ~40 uninterrupted minutes, which only exists for this couple in w5 (she's post-work energized while he's still up) and w7 (Saturday, both free) — tagged narrowly on purpose since a mid-game abandon is a bad experience.

gaps: NYT Games (Wordle/Connections/Spelling Bee) 'add friends and compare streaks' feature: widely reported to exist, but nytimes.com blocked automated fetching and the web search budget was exhausted before an official help.nytimes.com source could be located. Excluded from the activity list per the never-invent-a-source rule rather than included on secondary hearsay. Recommend a human quickly check help.nytimes.com/games directly — this is a strong likely W2/W4/W8/W9 candidate if confirmed.

Codenames: Duet online: only a secondary article (boardgamequest.com) confirms a digital Duet implementation exists; could not confirm which specific URL currently hosts a live, working Duet ruleset (as opposed to base team-mode Codenames, which most free web clones implement instead). Included at confidence: low — verify before shipping.

Apple does not publish a static, comprehensive list of SharePlay-supported games; the only way to get ground truth is opening FaceTime on-device and scrolling the live SharePlay app list. This is why apple_shareplay is 'unknown' for the large majority of entries in this thread rather than a guess either way.
Heads Up!'s SharePlay support is confirmed only against Apple's 2021 launch-partner announcement; not independently re-verified against a 2026-dated source that the integration still functions today.

IL vs US App Store region/price checks were only fully completed for GamePigeon (confirmed live on the Israeli App Store, priced in ILS — GamePigeon+ ₪17.90). Chess.com, Words With Friends 2, Wordfeud, GeoGuessr, Heads Up!, and Netflix Games' Israeli pricing were NOT individually re-verified this session; general-audience apps are unlikely to be region-locked, but exact ILS pricing (especially GeoGuessr Pro and Netflix subscription tiers) is unconfirmed.

GamePigeon's individual minigame mechanics (exact Word Hunt/Anagrams timer length, precise turn structure) were confirmed only at the level of 'this game exists in the collection' via the app's own store listing, not independently play-tested.
Board Game Arena's per-game Premium ($3/mo) tier requirements are unclear — could not confirm whether Splendor Duel or 7 Wonders Duel specifically require Premium or are fully free.

No reddit.com/r/LongDistance or r/iosgaming permalinks were successfully retrieved this session (site-restricted searches returned no on-topic results — likely an indexing gap, not necessarily an absence of such threads). All 16 entries are sourced from official/vendor documentation instead, which is a stronger source tier per the anti-slop mandate, but the brief's 'real couples describe a specific ritual' angle is unfulfilled for this thread.

Stardew Valley mobile multiplayer was investigated and deliberately excluded: as of the 1.6 mobile update, cross-device online play requires manual IP-address connection with no matchmaking/discovery, making it impractical for two people on different continents without extra networking setup (port forwarding or a relay service). A legitimate negative finding, not an oversight.

Gartic Phone was investigated and deliberately excluded: technically playable with 2 (no hard minimum), but the game's core 'broken telephone' mechanic depends on longer chains of players (4+ recommended); with exactly 2 it collapses into a much weaker loop. Noted per the 'many party games need 3+, say so' instruction rather than padded into the list.
confidence_summary: Overall MEDIUM-HIGH. The asynchronous/correspondence core (9 of 16 entries: Chess.com, Words With Friends 2, Wordfeud, the three GamePigeon bundles, Board Game Arena's Splendor Duel, and both Duolingo formats) is sourced directly from official app listings, Chess.com's and BGA's own help/FAQ pages, and Duolingo's own blog — high confidence and the strategic core of this thread. The real-time browser games (skribbl.io, PlayingCards.io, GeoGuessr, Netflix's Exploding Kittens, BGA's 7 Wonders Duel) are sourced from the vendor's own site or app listing — high-to-medium confidence. Two entries are explicitly lower-confidence and flagged in gaps: Codenames Duet online (LOW) and Heads Up! SharePlay (MEDIUM, 2021-era source). Apple's SharePlay status could not be verified for most entries because Apple does not publish a static supported-games list — reported honestly as 'unknown' rather than guessed, per the sourcing mandate.
thin_window_note: T3 fully covers W2, W4, W8, and W9 — the nine asynchronous/correspondence entries (Chess.com, WWF2, Wordfeud, GamePigeon's three game bundles, Board Game Arena's turn-based Splendor Duel, and both Duolingo formats) are explicitly designed to be playable in a single unscheduled minute at any point in either partner's day, which is exactly what these four thin windows need. T3 CANNOT serve W3 (her hands-busy, screen-free commute) — every entry in this thread requires at least glancing at a screen to make a move or read a board, which structurally rules out 'eyes on the road/transit, hands busy' use. This thread does not fake a W3 fit anywhere; W3 correctly belongs to T1 (audio-only co-listening) and T4 (verbal games). Within W4 specifically, four entries (GamePigeon's three bundles plus Netflix Games Exploding Kittens) meet the stricter 'discreet, desk/public-safe, no loud audio' bar explicitly requested by the cross-cutting quota — satisfying that sub-requirement using W4 alone, since this thread does not own W3.
